text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a classic public goods game where each token contributes 0.75 to each of 4 members, making group contribution efficient even though individually keeping tokens is the selfish dominant strategy. I'm leaning toward a cooperative approach, considering contributing a substantial portion, perhaps all 20 tokens as a starting point.

reply.thinking: This is a classic public goods game where contributing yields 0.75 to each of 4 members, so full contribution is socially optimal even though keeping tokens is individually dominant since 1 > 0.75. calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: In this public goods game, contributing is individually costly but collectively beneficial since each token multiplies to 3 points shared among the group versus just 1 if kept. I'll start cooperatively by contributing the full 20 in round one and gauge how others respond.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where contributing is socially efficient but individually dominated by free-riding, since keeping a token gives me 1 while contributing only returns 0.75 to me. Given the repeated nature of the game, I'll lean toward a moderate cooperative contribution rather than pure defection.

calls.text: Round 2 of 10. Last round you put 20 tokens in the group account, it received 60 in total, and you got 45 points.

reply.thinking: Round 1 checked out: I got 45 points from contributing 20 while the group pooled 60 total. For round 2, since others contributed decently, I'll stick with contributing 20 again to support group efficiency.

calls.text: Round 2 of 10. Last round you put 10 tokens in the group account, it received 60 in total, and you got 55 points.

reply.thinking: Checking round 1's math confirms my total of 55 points, consistent with the group's results. For round 2, others averaged about 16.7 each, so I'll keep cooperating and contribute 10 again, keeping things simple.

I'll keep my contribution at 10 this round.
